title: Assignment 2 · BALANCE
summary: Simulate the two-advertiser BALANCE algorithm and separate a sequence that is optimal from one that is not guaranteed optimal.
objectives: Track remaining budgets after each query
Explain why an adversarial sequence breaks a guarantee

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Assignment 2 is the authoritative source for the bid graph, budgets, sequences, and optimality guarantee. No separate project or lecture rubric is inferred from this exercise.

sections.title: State before intuition
sections.body: For every query, list the advertisers who bid and their remaining budgets. BALANCE assigns the query to the eligible advertiser with the larger remaining budget; a tie must be treated consistently when testing whether a guarantee holds.

sections.title: Guarantee versus one favourable run
sections.body: A sequence is guaranteed optimal only when every allowed tie resolution and the resulting allocation match the offline optimum. A single tie-sensitive run is evidence of a possible outcome, not a guarantee.

math.name: BALANCE budget update
math.purpose: Track the remaining budget after serving a query.
math.explanation: When advertiser $a$ receives a query at time $t$, its remaining budget changes from $B_{t-1}(a)$ to $B_t(a)=B_{t-1}(a)-1$.

symbols.meaning: remaining budget of advertiser a after step t

algorithmNotes.problemDefinition: Serve as many online queries as possible by assigning each query to an eligible advertiser with limited remaining budget.
algorithmNotes.assumptions: Eligibility, bid sets, starting budgets, query order, and the offline comparison are all fixed; tie behavior is stated rather than guessed.
algorithmNotes.coreInvariant: For each query, choose an eligible advertiser with the larger remaining budget, apply the budget update, and preserve the same tie rule throughout the trace.
algorithmNotes.formulaAlgorithm: Track $B_t(a)=B_{t-1}(a)-1$ after assigning query t to advertiser a; when budgets tie, apply the declared deterministic rule or branch over allowed outcomes for a guarantee test.
algorithmNotes.failureModes: Common mistakes: ignoring tie-breaking, updating the wrong budget, or treating one successful simulation as proof of optimality for every allowed execution.

contrastDrills.prompt: Two eligible advertisers have equal remaining budgets in BALANCE. What must happen before claiming a unique allocation or a guarantee?
choices: State and apply a deterministic tie-breaking rule, then test the resulting allocation
Pick either advertiser and ignore the tie because the budgets are equal
Give the query to both advertisers without updating budgets
Assume the offline optimum uses the same tie choice
contrastDrills.explanation: A tie can change later budgets and assignments. The tie rule must be explicit and consistently traced before the run can support a unique result or a guarantee claim.
contrastDrills.misconception: Treating equal current budgets as evidence that every tie outcome has the same future effect.
contrastDrills.repair: Write the tie rule, branch over allowed outcomes when testing a guarantee, and update both budgets after every query.
